text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The National Assembly's deputy chairman, Phung Van Tuu, died on Thursday after a long illness.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has told Haiphong's authorities that they need to be much more adventurous in turning the port city into a key industrial center of northern Vietnam.

-- The State Bank of Vietnam said new measures would be implemented to assist the banking system in the second half of 1997, including the application of open market operations, a revision of regulations on legal reserves and the application of forward transactions and swaps.
-- Electricity of Vietnam is preparing to take out loans from the World Bank for a $200-million project to build the country's second 500KV power transmission line.
-- Vietnam and Laos celebrated the 20th anniversary of their friendship and cooperation treaty in Hanoi on Thursday.
-- Vietnam has set a target of $5 billion for exports this year.

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has called on Vietnamese living in China's Yunnan province to contribute to consolidating friendship and multi-faceted relations between Vietnam and China.
-- Moslems in Ho Chi Minh City celebrated of the Prophet Muhammad's birthday (Maulid) on Thursday.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's police have solved 531 drug cases involving 1,845 people in the last eight months.
